name: 3d-scene-recipe
title: A lit 3D shape you can drag to turn, by hand
summary: The 3D recipe written out: a window-filling canvas, clearDepth3D, a perspective camera3D whose distance follows the aspect, two directional lights, one meshPrimitive3D torus, a matrix3D chain of tilt and spin driven by two touchExpressions, a theme paint colour and drawMesh3D; in mono a hidden-line wireframe instead.
prompt: Show one 3D shape, lit, that I can drag to turn; write the camera, the lights and the transforms out so I can see how 3D works.
hand_built: The ops themselves are the lesson. For a scene of several parts, a product turntable or an assembly, call Scene3D: it frames the camera at every angle and aspect, places parts by size and position, and adds autorotate, assembly and the mono look.
teaches: The order: clearDepth3D, camera3D, lights3D, meshPrimitive3D (an id), then per draw: matrix3D identity and its chain, a paint colour, drawMesh3D of that id
The 3D viewport is the whole window, drawn at the canvas's top left: make the 3D canvas fill the window, and give camera3D aspect componentWidth() / componentHeight()
Frame for the narrow side: eye distance = d * max(1, componentHeight() / componentWidth()), so a portrait window moves the camera back as much as it narrows the view

Orbit: two touchExpressions on touchX() and touchY() (stopMode gently, so a release coasts) become angles in radians for matrix3D rotate about X (tilt) and Y (spin); clamp tilt with the touch's min and max
matrix3D ops post-multiply: identity, rotate X, rotate Y, then the mesh; angles are radians
Lights are directions the light travels (down and into the screen is [x, -y, -z]); the colour is the paint colour, lit by 0.2 ambient plus each light's |N.L| times its intensity
Mono: {"$if": "theme.mono"} in the commands picks a hidden-line wireframe (drawMesh3D wireframe, edges [0, 1] draws the quads without diagonals) in onSurface instead of the lit fill
pitfalls: 3D support has not landed in androidx yet (coming): this plays in the C++ and TypeScript players only, and the Java JSON parser drops the 3D operations. Don't use it for a screen that must play on Android today

A 3D canvas that does not start at the window's top left, or does not fill it, draws its scene off-centre and outside its box: the players draw into a window-sized buffer placed at the canvas's origin
matrixSave / matrixRestore do not save the 3D matrix: start each object's chain again with matrix3D identity
matrix3D needs an op; {"translate": [x, y, z]} is an error, write {"op": "translate", "x": .., "y": .., "z": ..}
Lighting is two-sided Lambert with a fixed 0.2 ambient and colours multiply: a dark theme colour stays dark, and lights brighter in sum than about 1.2 wash a light colour out to white

snippets.note: camera3D: perspective, fovY 0.6 rad, aspect from the canvas, eye distance from a variable
lights3D: a warm key light from the upper left, a cool fill from the right
meshPrimitive3D torus: major and minor radius, 32 segments, built by the player
touchExpression on touchX(): the drag accumulates and coasts; it becomes the spin angle

check.describe: A blue ring (torus) seen from above at an angle, lit from the upper left, centred and filling about 80% of the width. Dark: a lighter blue on the dark background. Mono: the ring as a black (mono light) or white (mono dark) grid of quads with hidden lines removed. Turned: seen from another side and higher.

java_difference: 3D support has not landed in androidx yet (coming): the Java JSON parser does not know camera3D, lights3D, matrix3D, meshPrimitive3D or drawMesh3D; plays in the C++ and TypeScript players
